changes.text: 魏安釐王二十年，秦军围邯郸，魏王遣晋鄙救赵，却因畏秦令晋鄙停军于邺观望，平原君的使者责问魏救不至。魏公子决意赴秦军而死，路过夷门辞别后又折返，被一个守门老人当面点破：那是拿肉投餒虎。本文看他如何在没有干净选项时准备、付代价、认亏欠。

In the twentieth year of King Anxi of Wei, Qin's armies closed around Handan and the king of Wei sent General Jin Bi to relieve Zhao, but, fearing Qin, had him halt at Ye and wait to see which way things went; Lord Pingyuan's envoys complained that Wei's relief had not come. The Wei prince resolved to go and die at the Qin army; after taking his leave at the Yimen gate and riding off, he turned back, and an old gatekeeper told him to his face that this was meat thrown to a starving tiger. Here is how he worked the problem when no option was clean — what he prepared, what it cost, and what he admitted he owed.

魏安釐王二十年，秦军击破赵长平军之后，进兵围住邯郸。魏王派将军晋鄙带十万众救赵。秦王随即遣使警告魏王：攻赵旦暮可下，诸侯有敢救赵的，拔赵之后必先移兵击之。魏王恐惧，派人叫晋鄙停军，驻扎在邺，「名為救趙，實持兩端以觀望」。赵国平原君（赵惠文王之弟）的使者冠盖相属，赶到魏国，责让这位魏国公子：平原君说，自己之所以与公子结为婚姻，是看重公子的高义，以为公子能急人之困；如今邯郸旦暮之间就要降秦，而魏国的救兵至今不到，公子能急人之困又在哪里？末了还添一句「獨不憐公子姊邪」。魏公子的姐姐，正是平原君夫人。难处在于：救兵听命于魏王，而魏王畏秦，按兵不动。

In the twentieth year of King Anxi of Wei, after Qin had broken Zhao's army at Changping, its armies pressed on and encircled Handan. The king of Wei sent General Jin Bi with a hundred thousand troops to relieve Zhao. The king of Qin then sent an envoy to warn the king of Wei that Zhao would fall any day, and that whichever of the lords dared to relieve it, Qin would turn its troops on first once Zhao was taken. The king of Wei, afraid, sent orders halting Jin Bi, who encamped at Ye — nominally relieving Zhao, in fact keeping a foot in both camps and waiting to see. Envoys from Lord Pingyuan of Zhao (younger brother of King Huiwen of Zhao) arrived in Wei one after another — caps of office and carriage canopies in an unbroken line — reproaching this prince of Wei: Lord Pingyuan said he had joined himself to the prince by marriage because he valued the prince's high sense of duty and believed him a man who would rush to others in distress; now Handan was within days of surrendering to Qin, and Wei's relief still had not come — where, then, was that readiness to rush to others in distress? They added, in translation: had he no pity for his own sister? The prince's elder sister was Lord Pingyuan's wife. The difficulty: the relief army answered to the king of Wei, and the king, fearing Qin, kept it standing still.
此时公子手里有三千门客，却未被任以国政。他多次请魏王出兵，宾客辩士也「說王萬端」，魏王畏秦，终不听。公子自度终不能说动魏王，不肯独自活着而坐视赵亡，于是约车骑百余乘，打算带门客赴秦军，与赵俱死。出城路过夷门时，他向夷门守门人侯嬴（下称侯生）辞决。

At this point the prince had three thousand retainers but no appointment to the governance of the state. He petitioned the king of Wei again and again, and his guests and persuaders argued with the king in every way; the king, fearing Qin, would not listen. Judging that he could never win the king over, and unwilling to live on while Zhao perished, he gathered a hundred-odd carriages and horsemen, meaning to go with his retainers to the Qin army and die together with Zhao. On his way out of the city, passing the Yimen gate, he took his leave of Hou Ying, the gatekeeper of the Yimen.
一种解释是，这件事两面都算数：公子的信息能力得到验证，代价也记在账上——「是後魏王畏公子之賢能，不敢任公子以國政」。他越能干，魏王越不敢把国政交给他。等到邯郸告急，他没有国政之任，只能一再请王出兵；而原文给出的魏王终不听的缘由，是「魏王畏秦」。

One reading is that the episode cuts both ways. His intelligence was proven — and the price went straight onto the ledger: in translation, from then on the king of Wei feared the prince's ability and dared not entrust him with the government of the state. The more capable he appeared, the less his king would hand him. By the time Handan cried for help he held no charge of the governance of the state and could only petition the king to send troops, again and again; and the reason the source gives for the king's refusal is his fear of Qin.
侯生后来把话说穿：他故意让公子的车骑久立市中，让过客围观，公子愈恭，于是「市人皆以嬴為小人，而以公子為長者能下士也」。他还推荐过一位屠者朱亥，说「此子賢者，世莫能知」。公子几次登门去请，朱亥不回谢，公子当时只觉得奇怪。作者认为，这些看似闲棋的往来，邯郸被围那年全用上了。

Hou Ying later spelled out the game he had been playing. He had deliberately left the prince's carriage standing in the marketplace so that passers-by could watch: the longer the prince waited, the more deferential he became — and so, he said in translation, the townsfolk all took Hou Ying for a petty man, and the prince for a true elder who could humble himself before men of talent. He also recommended a butcher named Zhu Hai, calling him, in translation, a worthy man whom the world did not know. The prince called on Zhu Hai several times; the butcher never came to return the courtesies, which the prince at that point simply found odd. In the author's view, all of these seemingly idle moves came due in the year Handan was besieged.
平原君的使者在魏国把话说绝：救兵不到，公子的高义安在。他多次请魏王，宾客辩士也百般劝说，魏王终不听；公子「自度終不能得之於王」，这才决意赴秦军而死。

Lord Pingyuan's envoys left nothing to the imagination in Wei: with no relief army in sight, where was the prince's famed righteousness? He petitioned the king of Wei again and again, and his guests and persuaders argued every angle, but the king would not listen; only when the prince judged that he could never win the king over did he resolve to go and die against the Qin army.
那天他出城，路过夷门，见到侯生，把要去秦军送死的打算讲了，辞决而行。侯生只说一句「公子勉之矣，老臣不能從」。车行数里，公子心不快——这是《史记》的叙述用语——说：「吾所以待侯生者備矣，天下莫不聞，今吾且死而侯生曾無一言半辭送我，我豈有所失哉？」他「復引車還，問侯生」。

That day he rode out, passed the Yimen gate, stopped to see Hou Ying and told him the whole plan — going to die at the Qin army — then took his leave and set off. Hou Ying said only, in translation, that the prince should push on, and that this old servant could not follow him. A few li on, the prince felt displeased — the narrator's own phrase — and said, in translation, that he had treated Hou Ying handsomely in every way, as all the world knew; now he was going to his death, and Hou Ying had not half a word to see him off — had he fallen short somewhere? So he turned his carriage around and went back to question Hou Ying.
作者认为，这一折返是全篇的转折。侯生当面把话挑明：「今有難，無他端而欲赴秦軍，譬若以肉投餒虎，何功之有哉」——没有别的办法，只想冲进秦军，等于拿肉喂饿虎，白送，还要门客何用。他还说，公子待他厚，此去而他不相送，公子必会「恨之復返」。他自己说：「以是知公子恨之復返也」。

In the author's reading, that turn is the pivot of the whole story. Hou Ying put it to his face, in translation: with disaster upon him and no other plan, the prince meant to throw himself at the Qin army — like throwing meat to a starving tiger; what would it accomplish? Nothing gained — and what use, then, are retainers? He added that the prince had treated him well, and he had not seen the prince off; from this, he said, he had known the prince would resent it and come back.
侯生给出的方案：他说，晋鄙的兵符常在魏王卧内，如姬最幸，出入卧内，有办法窃取。他又说，如姬的父亲被人所杀，三年未能报仇，自王以下想替她报父仇的都没能做到；她曾向公子泣诉，公子使客斩了仇人的头敬献给她。侯生说如姬「欲為公子死，無所辭，顧未有路耳」，所以公子开口请她，她必许。得虎符、夺晋鄙军，北救赵而西却秦，「此五霸之伐也」。公子从其计，去请如姬，「如姬果盜晉鄙兵符與公子」。

Hou Ying's plan, as he laid it out: Jin Bi's army tally — a tiger tally — was normally kept in the king of Wei's bedchamber, and Lady Ruji, the king's favorite, came and went there and was able to steal it. He went on: her father had been murdered; for three years she had sought revenge, and no one, from the king down, had been able to avenge him. She had wept to the prince, who sent a retainer to cut off her enemy's head and presented it to her respectfully. Hou Ying said she was ready to die for the prince and would refuse him nothing; only, in translation, she had not yet had the opportunity. If the prince would but ask, she would certainly agree. Then, with the tiger tally in hand, he could seize Jin Bi's army, relieve Zhao in the north and drive Qin back in the west — in translation, an achievement to rank with the Five Hegemons. The prince followed the plan and asked Lady Ruji; she did indeed steal Jin Bi's army tally and give it to him.

计策只管前半，后半是坏情况。侯生提醒「將在外，主令有所不受」：就算合符成功，晋鄙不交兵权、再向魏王请示，事情就危险了。带上屠者朱亥，「晉鄙聽，大善；不聽，可使擊之」。公子听完流泪，说「晉鄙嚄唶宿將，往恐不聽，必當殺之，是以泣耳，豈畏死哉」——哭的是非杀本国老将不可，不是怕死。朱亥说自己是市井鼓刀屠者，从前不回谢是以为小礼无所用，「今公子有急，此乃臣效命之秋也」。侯生此前已说过老臣不能从，这里只请数着公子的行程，到晋鄙军那天「北鄉自剄，以送公子」。后来公子到了军中，「侯生果北鄉自剄」。

The plan covered only the first half; the second half was the bad case. Hou Ying warned, in translation, that a general in the field does not accept every order from his sovereign: even with the tallies matching, if Jin Bi withheld the army and sent to the king instead, the whole enterprise would be in danger. So take the butcher Zhu Hai along: if Jin Bi obeyed, excellent; if not, Zhu Hai could be made to strike him. The prince wept on hearing it; in translation, he said Jin Bi was a battle-seasoned old general who he feared would not obey, and then he would have to be killed — that was why he wept, not because he feared death. What he cried for was the killing of his own country's veteran commander, not the risk to himself. Zhu Hai said he was a butcher who wielded the knife in the marketplace; he had never returned the prince's visits because he thought petty courtesies were of no use — but now that the prince was in need, this was his moment to give his life. Hou Ying, who had already said at the gate that he could not follow, here only asked to count the days of the journey, so that on the day the prince reached Jin Bi's camp he would face north and cut his own throat, to see him off. When the prince did reach the army, Hou Ying did indeed face north and cut his own throat.
公子到邺，矫魏王令代晋鄙。晋鄙合符之后起了疑心，举手看着公子质问：自己拥十万之众屯于境上，是国之重任，如今公子单车来代，这算什么？他「欲無聽」——侯生预想的坏情况果然出现。朱亥袖中四十斤铁椎，椎杀晋鄙。公子遂将晋鄙军，随即勒兵下令：「父子俱在軍中，父歸；兄弟俱在軍中，兄歸；獨子無兄弟，歸養。」得选兵八万人，进兵击秦军。

At Ye the prince, on a forged royal order, moved to replace Jin Bi. Jin Bi matched the tallies but grew suspicious; raising his hand and looking at the prince, he asked, in translation, what it meant that he, holding a hundred thousand men on the frontier — a weighty charge of state — was now to be replaced by a man arriving with a single carriage. He was minded not to obey: the bad case Hou Ying had foreseen had come to pass. Zhu Hai, with a forty-catty iron mallet in his sleeve, struck Jin Bi dead. The prince then took command of Jin Bi's army and immediately issued an order to the troops, here in translation: where father and son were both serving, the father should go home; where brothers were both serving, the elder should go home; an only son with no brothers should go home and support his parents. He selected eighty thousand men and advanced against the Qin army.

赵孝成王感念公子矫夺晋鄙兵存赵，与平原君商量以五城相封。公子的反应是「意驕矜而有自功之色」——仍是叙述用语。门客劝他：别人对公子的恩不可忘，公子对别人的恩最好忘掉；况且矫魏王令、夺晋鄙兵救赵，「於趙則有功矣，於魏則未為忠臣也」，自骄而居功，不可取。公子立自责，似若无所容者。后来赵王洒扫亲迎，执主人之礼，公子侧行辞让，「自言罪過，以負於魏，無功於趙」；赵王侍酒至暮，因公子退让，终究没有开口献出五城。

King Xiaocheng of Zhao, grateful that the prince had seized Jin Bi's army on a forged royal order and saved Zhao, took counsel with Lord Pingyuan about granting him five cities. The prince's reaction, in the narrator's phrasing (here in translation), was a look of pride and self-congratulation. A retainer told him: some things must not be forgotten, others must be. Kindness done to the prince he should remember; kindness the prince had done to others, he should forget. And besides, forging the king of Wei's order and seizing Jin Bi's army to save Zhao was, in translation, a service to Zhao but not the act of a loyal minister to Wei — to swagger over such a credit was beneath him. The prince at once blamed himself, looking as if he had nowhere to hide. Later, when the king of Zhao swept the way, received him in person and performed the rites of a host, the prince stepped aside and declined, confessing, in translation, that he had wronged Wei and had no merit in Zhao; the king of Zhao served him wine until dusk but, because the prince held back so, never brought himself to offer the five cities.
魏王怒公子盗兵符、矫杀晋鄙，公子自己清楚。在原文的叙述里，下面这件事排在赵王议封五城之前：退秦存赵之后，他派将领率军归魏，自己与门客留在赵国。这场救赵中盗符夺军、矫杀晋鄙的一段没有魏王的授权。

The king of Wei was furious that the prince had stolen his tally and killed Jin Bi on a forged order, and the prince knew it. In the source's narration, what follows comes before the king of Zhao's discussion of the five cities: having driven off Qin and saved Zhao, he had a general lead the army back to Wei and stayed behind in Zhao with his retainers. The part of the rescue of Zhao in which he stole the tally, seized the army and killed Jin Bi carried no royal authorization.
第二处是把坏情况写进计划。侯生提醒将在外、主令有所不受，于是朱亥随行、袖中藏椎，晋鄙听则已，不听则击。作者推断，这一步的难处不在敢不敢：公子听后的反应是流泪说，怕晋鄙不听，到时必须杀他，自己并非怕死。作者认为，从结果看，他欠了自己这方一笔债——杀本国宿将、盗王符、惹魏王怒——仍然把方案走完。原文未写他事前是否权衡，能记的只有这句答话。

The second undignified spot is writing the bad case into the plan. Hou Ying's reminder that a general in the field need not accept every order put Zhu Hai at his side with a mallet up his sleeve: if Jin Bi complied, well; if not, strike. The author's inference: the hard part here was not daring. The prince's response on hearing the plan was tears — he said he feared Jin Bi would not obey, and that he would then have to be killed, and that he was not afraid to die. In the author's view, judging by the outcome, he took on a debt to his own side — killing his country's veteran commander, stealing the king's tally, angering the king — and he went through with it anyway. Whether he weighed this beforehand goes unrecorded; the only thing on the record is that answer.

第三处是事后的账。门客那句「於趙則有功矣，於魏則未為忠臣也」把两边算清：功劳是赵国的，亏欠是魏国的。原文记他受劝后立即自责，又在赵王面前侧行辞让，自言负魏、无功于赵，赵王因此终未献五城。至于留赵，原文叙在五城之议之前，紧接在魏王之怒与「公子亦自知也」之后；后文又记他「留趙十年不歸」，魏王派使者来请时，他「恐其怒之」，告诫门下敢替魏王使者通报者死。一种解释是，他以留在赵国、不回魏国的方式认下了这笔债；但照原文，留赵也可能出于躲避魏王之怒，这一解读只能存疑。作者认为，他真正把这笔债说出口，是辞让五城时自言负魏的那一刻。

The third is the accounting afterward. The retainer's words — in translation, a service to Zhao but not the act of a loyal minister to Wei — keep both columns straight: the credit belongs to Zhao, the debt to Wei. The source records that he blamed himself at once when rebuked, and that before the king of Zhao he stepped aside and declined, saying he had wronged Wei and had no merit in Zhao, so that the king never offered the five cities. As for staying in Zhao, the source narrates it before the five-city offer, directly after the king of Wei's anger and the note that the prince knew of it; later it records that he stayed in Zhao for ten years without returning, and that when the king of Wei sent envoys to ask for him, he feared the king's anger and warned his household that anyone who passed on a message from the king's envoys would die. One reading is that he acknowledged the debt by staying in Zhao rather than returning to Wei; but on the source's own account, staying in Zhao may equally have been a way of avoiding the king's anger, so that reading must remain tentative. In the author's view, the moment he actually spoke the debt aloud was when he declined the five cities and admitted he had wronged Wei.
今天最常见的版本是：团队看到明显风险，决策层迟迟不动。假设你已经在正常渠道反复争取过，仍然没有结果；你手里有一线证据，也有一个能干的人。先别急着感动自己——照侯生的话问一句，我这个动作是解决问题，还是拿肉投餒虎？如果只是冲出去把话说完、把人得罪完，而风险一点没减，那叫白送。

The commonest modern version: a team sees a clear risk, while the people with authority will not move. Suppose you have already pushed through the proper channels again and again, with no result; you hold a piece of hard evidence and you know a capable person. Before you start admiring your own nerve, put Hou Ying's question to your plan: is this move solving the problem, or throwing meat to a starving tiger? If all it does is get you out there to say your piece and offend everyone while the risk sits exactly where it was, that is a free throwaway.
细节上更该存疑的是：「得選兵八萬人」这个数字只此一处，无旁证；侯生自刭的缘由，原文只记他自言「以送公子」，没有更多交代。

The detail most worth doubting: the figure of eighty thousand picked men appears here alone, with no corroboration; as for why Hou Ying cut his throat, the source records only his own words that it was to see the prince off, and says nothing more.
本篇只有一个史源（《史记·魏公子列传》一处记述），对话与献计是史家记述，未必逐字；「心不快」「意驕矜」「立自責」是叙述用语而非实录心理；不换算公元年份；“得选兵八万人”仅此一处、无旁证。

This piece rests on a single historical source (one account in the Biography of the Wei Prince in the Records of the Grand Historian). The dialogue and the proposed scheme are the historian's rendering and need not be verbatim; the prince's displeasure, self-congratulation and self-blame are narrative labels rather than recorded psychology; years are not converted to the common era; the figure of eighty thousand picked men appears in this one place with no corroboration.
